title: Field repository: fields of a form in the IDE
summary: Reads the form in the editor into the field repository, or selects the persistent fields of a dataset from it; every change is checked before it is written
intro: Read this when the fields of the form you have open should go to the field repository, or should come from it. Each command is a dry run first; a list shows every change old and new, blocked changes cannot be checked, and only the checked changes are written.

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Field Repository > Read Fields from Dataset...
steps: Open the form (and the project that has the field repository); select the dataset in the designer, or pick it from the list
Choose drag-lint > Field Repository > Read Fields from Dataset...
Check the changes you want and press Apply (repo read-dfm --dataset --select)

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Field Repository > Read Fields of All Datasets of Form...
steps: Choose drag-lint > Field Repository > Read Fields of All Datasets of Form...
Check the changes you want and press Apply (repo read-dfm --select)

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Field Repository > Select Fields of Dataset...
steps: Open the form; select the dataset in the designer, or pick it from the list
Choose drag-lint > Field Repository > Select Fields of Dataset...
Check the fields the dataset should have and press Preview...
Check the changes you want and press Apply (repo write-dfm --names --select); the form is reloaded

surfaces.path: drag-lint > Field Repository > Copy Grid Columns...
steps: Choose drag-lint > Field Repository > Copy Grid Columns...
In 1.56 this row is a placeholder that only shows a message; the grid-copy lanes fill it

questions.ask: Which fields does the repository have for a dataset of a form, and which does the form have?
